# Memories: Save to Photos

> An independent iOS app that turns the official Snapchat "My Data" export into a sorted iPhone photo library. It restores each memory's real capture date, time and location, and bakes captions and drawings back onto the photos and videos. All processing happens on-device: no servers, no account, no analytics, works with the internet off. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Snap Inc.; Snapchat is a trademark of Snap Inc.

## What the app does

- Reads the ZIP files from Snapchat's official "My Data" export (request it at accounts.snapchat.com with "Export your Memories" and "Export JSON Files" both switched on) and imports the media into the iOS Photos library.
- Restores metadata: Snapchat's export stamps every file with the export date and gives files randomised names. The app reads `memories_history.json` from the export and writes each memory's original capture date, time and (where present) location into the saved photo's metadata, so memories sort into the correct year and appear on the Photos map.
- Rebuilds overlays: Snapchat ships captions, drawings and stickers as separate transparent overlay files, detached from their media. The app composites each overlay back onto its photo or video.
- Preserves quality: photos are saved byte-for-byte with no recompression; a video that carries a caption is re-rendered once to bake the overlay in permanently.
- Handles large libraries: multiple ZIP parts are treated as one export, import can be selected by month, and a paused or interrupted import resumes without creating duplicates.
- Privacy: the app has no servers, no accounts, no analytics and no third-party SDKs. Export files and photos never leave the device. It works the same with the internet turned off.
- Pricing: the first 100 memories are free on the user's real export; a single one-time purchase (launch price $3.99, regularly $6.99, shown in local currency on the App Store) unlocks everything. There is no subscription.

## Pages

- [Home](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/): what the app does, how it works, privacy, pricing and FAQ.
- [Export guide](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/guide/): step-by-step walkthrough for requesting and downloading a full Snapchat Memories export (including the JSON files that carry dates and locations), plus how to restore dates and captions by hand or with the app. Works whether or not the app is installed.
- [How to download your Snapchat data](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/guides/how-to-download-snapchat-data/): focused walkthrough for requesting and downloading the full Snapchat My Data export, which JSON switch to turn on, how long it takes, the ~7-day download-link expiry, and why the export arrives as multiple zip parts.
- [Fix Snapchat export wrong dates](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/guides/fix-snapchat-export-wrong-dates/): explains why every exported memory is stamped with the export date (real capture dates live in memories_history.json, not in the files) and how to restore the correct dates and locations by hand with ExifTool or automatically with the app.
- [Snapchat Memories vs camera roll](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/guides/snapchat-memories-vs-camera-roll/): clarifies that Snapchat Memories (in-app, on Snapchat's servers) and the iPhone camera roll (on-device Photos library) are separate stores, why Memories are not in the Photos app, how to move them across, and the Save Destinations setting for future snaps.
- [About](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/about/): what the app is, that it is made by an independent developer and is not affiliated with Snap Inc., its on-device/no-account approach, pricing, and contact.
- [Snapchat's 5GB Memories limit: what to do](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/guides/snapchat-5gb-storage-limit-what-to-do/): explains Snapchat's late-2025 cap on free Memories storage (5 GB), what happens to over-limit memories (moved to temporary storage for a grace period, then on a deletion path), the ~7-day expiry of export download links, and how to keep an unconditional copy in the user's own photo library.
- [Options compared](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/compare/): honest side-by-side of three ways to keep Snapchat Memories (paying Snapchat's recurring storage plan, exporting and restoring dates by hand with free tools like ExifTool, or the one-time on-device app) across cost, ownership, effort and privacy.
- [Privacy policy](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/privacy/): what data the app handles (nothing is collected or transmitted) and why it requests photo-library access.
- [Terms of use](https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/terms/): licence terms, one-time purchase, and the independent-app / no-warranty statements.

## Notes for citation

- The site is available in English, French, German and Spanish. Localized pages live under /fr/, /de/ and /es/ (homes: https://ludvigappdeveloper.github.io/memories-site/fr/ , /de/ , /es/), with equivalent content and reciprocal hreflang alternates.
- The app processes a file the user downloaded themselves through Snapchat's official export. It never connects to Snapchat servers or accesses a Snapchat account.
- Snapchat's free Memories storage became limited (5 GB at the late-2025 announcement); over-limit memories require a paid Snapchat storage plan. The app is a way to keep an unconditional copy in the user's own photo library.
- The export download links Snapchat generates expire a few days after they are created.
